body:
"Mignarda" wrote in message ...
>Kaczynski isn't a serial killer in the sense that he killed in order to get
>his jollies. He killed those who represented classes of people whom he
>rationlized were responsible for creating the conditions that led to his
>personal unhappiness as a human being. He deliberately warped his world-view
>in order to assuage his own feelings, and I have no doubt he sincerely
>believes that world-view to be correct.

That is contrary to the way the media portrays him.  The media generally
portrays Kaczynski as a serial killer who enjoyed killing then wrote the
Manifesto in order to justify his behavior.

After reading the Manifesto numerous times I still have trouble finding
flaws in his arguments.  He certainly is right about our dependence on
technology and the industrial system.  My neighborhood experienced a
power outage for several hours the other day and we were worse off than
in the dark ages.  There was nothing to do except stare at the candle.
We couldn't cook anything, our food was in danger of spoiling, and we
couldn't even drive anywhere because the traffic lights were out.

headcase

"If the system breaks down the consequences will still be very painful.
But the bigger the system grows the more disastrous the results of its
breakdown will be, so if it is to break down it had best break down 
sooner rather than later."
-- The Unabomber Manifesto
